content: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the symptoms are not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, it is essential to undergo regular laboratory and medical tests, including liver function tests, HIV RNA levels, blood sugar levels, complete blood counts, and cholesterol/triglyceride levels. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store unopened bottles of this medication in the refrigerator. Once the bottle is opened, the capsules can be stored at room temperature, but they must be kept away from light and moisture. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. After opening, the medication expires after 60 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Tipranavir must be administered with ritonavir to be effective. When these two drugs are combined, there have been rare but potentially fatal cases of severe liver problems. Additionally, patients taking tipranavir and ritonavir may rarely experience serious, sometimes fatal, bleeding in the brain (intracranial hemorrhage). This medication is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. Tipranavir belongs to a class of drugs called protease inhibitors and must be taken with ritonavir, another protease inhibitor, to boost its levels in the body. It is important to note that tipranavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Before starting tipranavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to sulfa drugs, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This drug may rarely cause an increase in blood sugar levels, potentially leading to or worsening diabetes. If you already have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. This medication may make you more sensitive to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and tipranavir may be part of that treatment. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of tipranavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin), rifampin, and others. Tipranavir with ritonavir can both speed up and slow down the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting how they work. Aspirin may increase the risk of bleeding when used with this medication. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams a day), continue taking it unless advised otherwise. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
